beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: The ink's dry on the contract. So, it turns out, is Riley's calendar — the label wants the songs held back for six months before anything comes out.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Six months of just sitting on it. After all that, waiting was not what I pictured happening next."

options.text: Sitting on it isn't the same as nothing happening.
Six months means they're punishing you for something.
Waiting periods don't actually mean anything.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I just feel like I'm losing momentum, stuck in place."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: You're suspended, not stuck — and it's calm, not suffering.
This card is a punishment for waiting too long.

elaboration: Suspended, upside down, but calm — not suffering, just paused. This isn't a penalty, it's a deliberate pause.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But I'm not doing anything differently just by sitting here."

options.text: A new perspective comes from surrendering to the pause, not fighting it.
You're right, you should be doing more right now.
This card has nothing to do with perspective.

elaboration: A new perspective comes from surrendering, not struggling — pause and let go instead of forcing the next move.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Maybe the six months isn't dead time. Maybe it's just time I haven't figured out the use of yet."
